title: Longitudinal clinical and micorbiological assessment of oral health in patients undergoing radiation in the head and neck area
summary:
Radiotherapy is often used to treat head and neck tumors. However, this can cause serious side effects in the oral cavity. The most important of these are osteoradionecrosis, which initially causes inflammation of areas of the jawbone and can eventually lead to the death of these areas. Inflammatory diseases of the periodontium and gums (periodontitis), which are mainly caused by bacteria, can play an important role in this process, but the relationship between radiation therapy, gum disease, and the oral microbiome has not yet been sufficiently researched.

Objective:
The study investigates how radiation therapy in the head and neck area affects the gums, the bacterial flora in the mouth, and the success of periodontitis treatment.

Methodology:
In a two-year observational study, 50 patients undergoing radiation therapy and 50 non-irradiated control subjects are monitored. At several points before, during, and after therapy, gum findings are recorded, the bacterial composition of dental plaque and saliva is examined, and quality of life is assessed. Patients with periodontitis receive standardized treatment and follow-up care. In addition, the relationship between the radiation dose and clinical and microbial changes is examined.

interventions.name: Observational group: Patients undergoing radiation in the head and neck area because of an HNSCC (head and neck squamous cell carcinoma)
Control: Patients with no anamnestic or planned radiation in the head and neck area

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Voluntary consent and written signature of the information sheet
At least five remaining teeth
Consent to regular participation in supportive periodontitis therapy at the Clinic for Conservative Dentistry and Periodontology for the duration of the study
Exclusion criteria:
Medication with bisphosphonates or Denosumab.
Second carcinoma in the head and neck area
